text:
Template v5 and its two builds are landed, on the person's words to this session "답 기다린 뒤 v5" [v5 after the answer has come] and on your reply 20261113-design-macbook-20261112-1-1 (73522c1). Template: 9f788b8 (meta_agent/src/build/template_v5, materialized as meta_agent/templates/agent@afb9ec0fb292). Builds: be84884 (meta_agent/builds/echo/0004, parent build-echo-0003; meta_agent/builds/rheo-fixture/0003, parent build-rheo-fixture-0002).

What v5 is: v4 with text changed in four files and no script changed (a test holds it to that). (a) tasks/001-start.md covers a scientific verdict of not_run as well as undecided and says neither is a pass. (b) The bundle's CLAUDE.md says envelope/safety.json holds one entry for each safety value the agent has, each null in a bundle, and that a file with no entry means no tool requires a gate, in your words. (f) CLAUDE.md and run-skill say the folder named runs is made by the session when it first writes there, and that an input nothing in the bundle gives is one line in failures.jsonl like a missing skill; run-skill has a section for it. (e) is the builder's, not the template's: src/build/bundle.py adds to the Subagents section of a build that has subagents that a skill that changes a device is run by operator only and that any other skill the session may run itself through the runner or give to the subagent that lists it. It is in rheo-fixture/0003 and not in echo/0004, which has no subagent.

Read off runs: validate.py --bundle on each of the two bundles printed VERDICT PASS mode=bundle, failed=0; session_skills.bundle_problems printed [] for each; the gate over the tree printed failed=0 with 7 bundles; meta_agent/tests ran 175 tests, OK; contracts/tests ran 75 tests, OK. Gates of the builds: echo/0004 interface pass, scientific undecided; rheo-fixture/0003 interface pass, scientific not_run. No session has been opened in either bundle.

(c) is not done, and one thing in your plan for it has to change because of that. The status contract is not a file of its own in the request: it is tools[4].contract of meta_agent/requests/req-rheo-fixture-001/intake.json, the A2 axis (spec_a2.json) lists the same three outputs, and the specification names that axis. A revised contract is therefore a new revision of the intake, of the axis and of the specification, and the designer has no mode that specifies an existing request again (--rebuild reads intake.json as it stands and writes no request card). That is a mechanism of its own, wanted for any request whose tool contract changes, and by the rule of 2026-11-11 it would have to run on two fixtures. It has no task card. So rheo-fixture/0003 is on v5 and carries the status contract as 0002 did, fault required and not declared. A check that binds bundles from the template version after v4 would fail that build, which is a record. I ask that the check bind from the version after v5, which is also where the runner's refusal of an undeclared output would go since it is a change of the template's code, or that you tell me another way.

Asked of you: (1) where the contract check binds, as above; (2) a task card, or a line in tasks/015, for specifying an existing request again when one of its tool contracts changes, if you want it; I start nothing on it without one. (d) and (g) stand as you answered.
